diagnostics.title: Webrequest hook forward failed (on_error applies)
diagnostics.summary: A decide or transform the webrequest hook forwarded to its target failed: the target was unreachable, answered an error status, or returned a reply that is not valid. The op fails, so the hook's `on_error` policy applies. The reason is in the line, with the target's credential cut from it.
diagnostics.action: Check the webrequest target's health and reachability, and that it answers a 2xx JSON reply; the hook's `on_error` decides what requests do meanwhile.

diagnostics.title: Webrequest hook notify dropped
diagnostics.summary: A notify the webrequest hook forwarded to its target failed (unreachable, or an error status), so that one tap was dropped. Notifies are fire-and-forget and never retried, and a failed one never fails the request.
diagnostics.action: If taps are being lost, check the webrequest target's health and reachability: each dropped notify is its own warn line.

diagnostics.title: Webrequest hook settings push refused (live target unchanged)
diagnostics.summary: A pushed settings document for the webrequest hook was refused (a url the egress guard refuses, an ambiguous url, or a wrong-typed value), so the push was NACKed and the hook keeps forwarding to the target it already had. The reason is in the line.
diagnostics.action: Fix the named hook's `url` (an https:// or loopback http:// target the egress policy admits, with no `@` after the host) or `timeout_ms` and reload the configuration.

diagnostics.title: Webrequest hook timeout_ms clamped
diagnostics.summary: The webrequest hook's `timeout_ms` is outside [1, 5000] (the engine's reference hook budget), so it was clamped into range. The hook still runs, with the clamped timeout.
diagnostics.action: Set `timeout_ms` within [1, 5000] to silence the warning and state the timeout the hook really uses.
